mechanism: Palace Model.Refinement.Boxes on the EXISTING mesh; no gmsh, no new mesh file
candidate_mesh_sha256: identical to baseline; the mesh file is an input, not regenerated

refinement_region.justification: the lumped-port face (attribute 10) bounding box padded by 0.010 mm, the same pad R1 declared, so the refined neighbourhood is comparable in extent while the mechanism is nested instead of a regenerated mesh

marking.criterion: any vertex of the element inside the closed box (geodata.cpp:282-306)

dof.why_not_measured: the refined mesh exists only inside Palace at load time. MFEM has no Python binding in this environment and Palace's --dry-run parses the config only (main.cpp:246-254), so no offline measurement is possible without reimplementing MFEM's bisection.
dof.lower_bound_derivation: marked submesh refines uniformly (octasection): E' = 2E+3F+T. Green closure only ADDS elements (mesh.cpp:10123), so E_total >= E_baseline + E(M) + 3F(M) + T(M).

invariants_by_construction.mesh_file: byte-identical; refinement is a config block
invariants_by_construction.existing_vertex_coordinates: never moved; new vertices are edge midpoints only (mesh.cpp:10834-10841)
invariants_by_construction.port_connectivity_and_L_s: w and l come from the bounding box of the port attribute (lumpedelement.cpp:22-69); midpoints are convex combinations of existing vertices, so the hull and hence w, l, L_s and kappa are unchanged
invariants_by_construction.Lc: largest mesh bounding-box extent; unchanged for the same reason

propagation.why: GeneralRefinement forces nonconforming=0 for 3D simplex meshes (mesh.cpp:10565-10567)
propagation.beyond_the_region: YES. Conformity is restored by a green-closure bisection loop (mesh.cpp:10123+) that refines adjoining elements outside the box. This is NOT a face-only or box-only change. Its extent is not computable offline and is the reason DOF cannot be pre-measured.
propagation.MaxNCLevels_and_Nonconformal: inert for tets; the conforming branch is taken first

quality.note: octasection of a tet is not quality-preserving in general; bisection quality is bounded by MFEM's marked-edge scheme but is not measured here
